transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-07
Start: 16:30 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees (Redwood): Jordan Patel (AE), Maya Chen (SE), Luis Ortega (Solutions Eng)
Attendees (Avalon): Priya Srinivasan (Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Security Architect), Samira Al-Khalil (Platform Lead), Ben Carter (CTO)
Shared artifacts: 1) Redwood SOC2 one-pager (link: https://redwood.example/soc2-summary), 2) Benchmark harness spreadsheet (link: drive/redwood/benchmarks/avalon), 3) Pilot runbook (short note)

Auto-generated summary (rough):
- Purpose: scope a 2-week pilot to validate performance and compliance requirements for Avalon: SOC2/ISO posture, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC and audit logging, and baseline latency/cost benchmarks.
- Success criteria discussed: p95 latency under 300ms for interactive queries, sustain 200 qps with 8k token context in deduced setup, end-to-end per-token cost estimate within target, and full audit log ingestion into customer's SIEM.
- Next steps: Redwood to provide docs + benchmark harness; Avalon to share traffic profile and schedule connectivity test.

Topics covered:
- Compliance baseline: SOC2 report, ISO27001 gap list, KMS/HSM options, data residency
- Auth: SSO/SAML flows, SCIM provisioning, RBAC mapping to Avalon AD groups
- Observability: audit logs retention, log format, push to Splunk/Datadog, syscall level vs app-level logs (some confusion on log granularity)
- Pilot sizing: concurrency, tokens/request, cold-start expectations, expected throughput for synthetic tests
- Benchmarks: p50/p95/p99 latency, per-token throughput, KV cache warm vs cold, quantized model variants for cost tradeoff
- Timeline: Pilot kickoff next Monday (two-week window) with mid-pilot checkpoint

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Um, I think we have about an hour to run through the pilot scope. I see the list of folks from Avalon, welcome.
[00:12] Priya (Avalon): Hi, thanks. We'll probably drop in a couple more engineers later but this is the core set.
[00:18] Marcus: Hi all. Our main ask up front is that whatever pilot we run, we need to be able to show to our security review that logs, SSO, and key management meet our controls.
[00:30] Jordan: Totally. That's the plan. Maya, do you want to take us through the security checklist and how Redwood supports it?
[00:36] Maya (Redwood SE): Sure. So high-level, we support SOC2 Type II reports, and we can share the AICPA summary. For pilots we typically provide the SOC2 bridge document and an ISO27001 statement of applicability — um, full ISO cert is customer-by-customer but we can map out controls. On auth, we have SAML SSO with SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows, SCIM for provisioning, and you can map RBAC roles to AD groups.
[01:05] Marcus: SCIM's critical for us, and we need audit logs pushed to Splunk with the identity context included (user, token id, route).
[01:12] Maya: Yep, we can emit audit events with user/email, request_id, model route, and token counts. For pilots we can configure log retention and a forwarder to your Splunk ingest endpoint or S3 if you prefer.
[01:24] Samira: What about encryption for keys? We must have customer-managed keys and HSM-backed KMS for production. For pilot, do you allow us to test with CMK?
[01:33] Luis (Redwood): For the Private deployment option we support bring-your-own-KMS (BYOK) with HSMs. In hosted pilots we can simulate KMS integrations and demonstrate envelope encryption; full BYOK is typically part of Dedicated/Private contracts but we can show a staging flow.
[01:49] Ben: Data residency — our compliance team will want logs and PII never leaving EU for EU customers. How is that handled?
[01:57] Maya: We have region pinning for hosted endpoints and the Private offering for on-prem or VPC deployments. For the pilot, if you want EU-only, we can spin a region instance in frankfurt region and confirm network egress controls. There may be additional setup time though.
[02:16] Priya: Okay good. Now on the performance side — our workload is chatty: roughly 220 requests per second at peak, average length 600 tokens, some rare long tail to 6k tokens. We'll want to size for p95 latency and cost.
[02:29] Jordan: That's helpful. For the pilot we generally ask for a representative sample: concurrency x token distribution. Maya, can you comment on how we'd size the dedicated pool for that?
[02:37] Maya: Sure — rough ballpark: for the model class you're asking about, assuming FP16 quantized variant, to hit 220 rps with 600 tokens you'd be looking at X GPUs (discussion had some back-and-forth, audio clipped). For an initial run, we recommend running a synthetic benchmark at 50% load then scale to full. We'll provide the benchmark harness where you can replay traffic.
[02:58] Marcus: We need to validate cold-cache vs warm. Our app relies heavily on prefix caching, so KV cache warm vs cold numbers are important.
[03:07] Luis: Absolutely. The harness can run warm-up phases to populate KV cache and then measure p95 and p99. We'll capture both per-token compute and end-to-end latency including network.
[03:18] Priya: What's the best success criteria phrasing for the security review? I want something I can put into the pilot acceptance criteria.
[03:24] Jordan: I'd propose: 1) SOC2 report reviewed and no open high-risk control gaps for pilot scope; 2) SSO with SCIM provisioning working end-to-end; 3) Audit logs forwarded to your SIEM containing identity and request metadata with retention configurable to 90 days; 4) Performance: p95 below 300ms for interactive subset and capability to sustain 200 qps at target token distribution; 5) Pilot runbook executed and documented.
[03:50] Ben: Is 300ms realistic with 6k contexts? That feels low.
[03:55] Maya: Right, for 6k tokens the p95 will be higher. We should split success criteria by class: interactive queries (<=800 tokens) p95 < 300ms, long-context batch queries (2k-8k) p95 < 1.2s. We can tailor the SLOs.
[04:10] Marcus: Ok that helps. On the logs payload format — can you include token-level counts and user identifiers without logging the actual content?
[04:18] Maya: Yes we can exclude content. Audit events will include metadata: token_count, model_id, route, request_id, user_email (if available) and a content hash only if you want it. We avoid logging PII by default.
[04:30] Samira: For SCIM we need group sync every 15 minutes roughly. Does Redwood support delta sync?
[04:35] Maya: We support SCIM with delta sync; polling cadence configurable. For pilot we'll set a shorter cadence.
[04:41] Priya: Let's talk benchmarks: what do you need from us to run a realistic run?
[04:44] Maya: A CSV of representative requests: timestamp, token_count, route, concurrency target. Also info on expected session affinity (do you pin users to sessions for chat?), and any specialized system prompts. We'll use the harness to replay at 50%, 75%, 100% of peak.
[04:58] Priya: We'll get that to you. How long to spin up the pilot infra?
[05:03] Jordan: If we do hosted in EU region, we can have a staging instance within 3 business days — full Private or BYOK will take longer (2-4 weeks). Pilot kickoff ideally next Monday; so a week to get initial artifacts and staging.
[05:15] Marcus: Network connectivity — we want mutual TLS to our VPC ingress and a secure peering for logs. Is that in scope?
[05:22] Luis: For Dedicated/Private, yes. For hosted, we use secured HTTPS endpoints and can provide a VPN tunnel or private link for the pilot with additional setup. We'll put a network runbook together.
[05:33] Ben: Any limitations on model variants you can run in the pilot? For cost comparisons we want a base model and a quantized one.
[05:40] Maya: We'll provide both variants: full precision and quantized (8-bit or 4-bit depending on model). The harness will report quality delta (we can run your eval set for regression checks).
[05:50] Jordan: Quick note — legal: we'll need an NDA and a DPA for processing. Samira, Marcus, do you want Redwood to kick off the simple NDA?
[05:58] Samira: Yes please, that speeds things.
[06:01] Marcus: Also, we'll need to involve our compliance reviewer before the pilot sign-off.
[06:05] Priya: On timelines, if we start next Monday, what's the check-in cadence?
[06:09] Jordan: Mid-pilot checkpoint at day 7 for initial performance report and security validation, final review at day 14 with a go/no-go. We'll also do daily standups if you want — maybe 15-min syncs first three days.
[06:20] Priya: Sounds good. A couple of clarifying items — will audit logs be tamper-evident? We need chain-of-custody for some events.
[06:27] Maya: We can sign logs with an integrity hash and push to S3 with object lock for the pilot if you need immutability, or integrate with your SIEM and turn on immutability on your side. We'll document options in the runbook.
[06:38] Ben: Great. Anything else?
[06:40] Jordan: We'll send an email recapping all artifacts, and Maya will share the benchmark harness link and a short runbook for the pilot. If that's fine we'll schedule the network deep-dive with Luis and your infra team for Thursday.
[06:51] Priya: Yes, please include the traffic sample template.
[06:54] Jordan: Okay, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with next steps and action items.
[07:00] Conversation winds down, misc chatter and names repeated, meeting ends.

Notes on transcription quality: Some timestamps clipped where multiple speakers talked over each other; a few technical terms transcribed slightly off (e.g., "K-V cash" instead of "KV cache" in one spot).

Pilot acceptance criteria (recap):
- Security: SOC2 summary reviewed; SSO/SAML + SCIM working; audit logs ingested to Splunk with retention 90d; KMS integration demonstrated for envelope encryption (BYOK demo ok for pilot).
- Performance: Interactive p95 thresholds and long-context thresholds defined (<=800 tokens p95 <300ms; 2k-8k p95 <1.2s); must sustain 200+ qps for representative workload in synthetic run.
- Operational: Runbook executed, network connectivity validated, and legal docs (NDA/DPA) signed.

References shared during call:
- SOC2 summary: https://redwood.example/soc2-summary
- Benchmark harness (drive): drive/redwood/benchmarks/avalon
- Pilot runbook (note): internal/redwood/pilot-runbooks/avalon

End of transcript.
